description: A chromatic quantizer that keeps its note until the incoming pitch has moved a set interval away from it, then takes the nearest semitone; two intervals are set and used in turn.

params.text: Sets the first interval, 0 to 11 semitones, snapped to whole numbers.
Sets the second interval, 0 to 11 semitones, snapped to whole numbers.

inputs.text: The pitch to be quantized, 1V/octave; the nearest semitone is taken whenever it has moved by the current interval or more from the note already being sent.
Sets the first interval from 0V for 0 semitones to 10V for 11 semitones, overriding the knob and turning it as it goes.
Sets the second interval from 0V for 0 semitones to 10V for 11 semitones, overriding the knob and turning it as it goes.

outputs.text: The quantized pitch, 1V/octave, held at the last note until the input has moved the current interval away from it.
A 10V trigger 1ms long each time a new note is quantized.

notes: Nothing comes out of either jack until a cable is in OUT. With OUT unpatched the quantizer is skipped altogether, so TRIGGER is left at whatever voltage it last held.
The intervals alternate: the first note change is allowed by interval 1, the next by interval 2, then interval 1 again. Which of the two is in force is not shown on the panel.
An interval of 0 semitones puts no distance between notes, so the input is requantized every sample and TRIGGER stays at 10V rather than pulsing.
Each display shows its interval as a number of semitones and its name, from Unison through to Major 7th. Neither can be clicked.
